# Supported platforms and cores

<!-- Generated by scripts/supported-platforms.mjs. Run npm run docs:platforms to update. -->

This is the complete platform, core and Target catalog declared by this checkout of retrom-runtime. On `master` it follows current development. To check an installed release, inspect the matching tag's catalog sources or this page when available. The host's installed runtime catalog determines the available integrations.

Catalog membership describes an integration, not compatibility with every game. Game formats, firmware, input and browser requirements depend on the selected Target. The [Target guides](README.md#target-guides) describe specific restrictions; [product acceptance records](acceptance/clean-refactor.md) retain the tested versions and evidence scope separately.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `emulatorjs` | 76 | 75 |
| `retrom-runtime` | 36 | 36 |

A platform is a hardware system or game-engine family. A `coreId` is the host-selectable core identity. A Target is identified by `providerId + targetId` and declares the actual runtime capabilities. A binding connects a core and its platforms/content kinds to one Target. These counts differ because one core can serve several platforms or Targets: RPG Maker has separate engine Targets, while Genesis Plus GX separates cartridge and CD execution.

## Bound Targets and save types

`INSTANT` restores an execution-state checkpoint in a new instance. `GAME_SAVE` transfers game-native save data and may require saving/loading through the game's menus. `NO_SAVE` means the Target offers no checkpoint. These are declared semantics; the acceptance records establish which game scenarios have actually been verified.

The Content column lists the accepted content kind and, where present, the required RPG Maker engine. Use the Target guides for file extensions and project layout; a project content kind does not accept arbitrary directories.

## Sources and maintenance

This page is generated from [`runtimeCatalog()`](../src/runtime/catalog.ts). The machine-readable sources are [platform names](../src/runtime/platforms.json), [core names](../src/runtime/core-names.json), [product bindings](../src/runtime/bindings.json), and the [EmulatorJS](../src/providers/emulatorjs/catalog.ts) / [native Web/Wasm](../src/providers/retrom-runtime/catalog.ts) Provider declarations. The acceptance matrix is a versioned evidence snapshot, not the current support inventory.

After changing these sources, regenerate and commit this page with the change:

```bash
npm ci
npm run docs:platforms
npm run docs:platforms:check
```

Both documentation commands compile the current runtime source before reading the catalog. They do not download or build third-party cores or Provider archives. The quality workflow checks that this page matches the catalog. Edit the generator for prose or layout changes.
